title: Three Ranges
statement: The integers $x$, $y$ and $z$ satisfy $-6 \le x \le 2$, $-5 \le y \le 3$ and $1 \le z \le 4$. What is the smallest possible value of the product $x \cdot y \cdot z$?
hints: Since $z$ is always positive, look at the sign of $x \cdot y$. Which signs must $x$ and $y$ have for the whole product to be negative? Notice that taking the largest sizes, $x = -6$ and $y = -5$, gives a positive product.
Use casework on the signs. For a negative product, $x$ and $y$ must have opposite signs, so either $x < 0 < y$ or $y < 0 < x$. In each case, find the largest possible size of $x \cdot y$.

If $x < 0 < y$, the most negative value of $x \cdot y$ is $(-6) \cdot 3 = -18$. If $y < 0 < x$, it is $2 \cdot (-5) = -10$. Since $z$ is positive, a larger $z$ makes a negative product more negative, so now choose $z$.
solution: We split into cases according to the signs of $x$ and $y$. Since $z \ge 1$, the number $z$ is always positive, so $x \cdot y \cdot z$ has the same sign as $x \cdot y$. If $x \cdot y \ge 0$, the product is not negative. For example, $x = -6$ and $y = -5$ have the largest sizes but give a positive product. So a negative product needs $x$ and $y$ to have opposite signs. Suppose first that $x < 0 < y$. Then $|x| \le 6$ and $|y| \le 3$, so $|x \cdot y| \le 18$. Suppose instead that $y < 0 < x$. Then $|x| \le 2$ and $|y| \le 5$, so $|x \cdot y| \le 10$. In both cases $|x \cdot y| \le 18$. Since $|z| \le 4$, every negative product satisfies $|x \cdot y \cdot z| \le 18 \cdot 4 = 72$, which means $x \cdot y \cdot z \ge -72$. Products that are not negative are certainly at least $-72$ too. This value is attained, because $x = -6$, $y = 3$, $z = 4$ satisfy all the ranges and give $(-6) \cdot 3 \cdot 4 = -72$. The smallest possible value of the product is $-72$. Why this works. casework, bounding: splitting on the signs of $x$ and $y$ leaves only two patterns that can give a negative product, and in each one the size of the product is bounded by the largest allowed sizes.
